attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No theorem yet converts an arbitrary SAT-semantic nonfunctional certificate into either a functional natural property or a sparse-row residual circuit. The row gate is a necessary falsifier audit, not a complete proof-system lower-bound framework.
steps: Fix H_N^{SAT}(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)) with M_N=N^{q+o(1)}, L_N=(log N)^d, and C(G_N)<=N^{rho+o(1)}.
Assume SAT has circuits of size n^c at length L_N. Substituting the same SAT circuit into every generated slot gives C(H_N^{SAT})<=N^{rho+o(1)}+N^{q+o(1)}L_N^c.
Since L_N^c=N^{o(1)}, the transfer is N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}. Therefore C(H_N^{SAT})>N^{1+epsilon} with max{rho,q}<1+epsilon implies SAT notin SIZE(n^c) for every fixed c.

Now suppose a residual circuit D_N of size S_D agrees with H_N^{SAT} outside R_N, with |R_N|=E_N. For each exceptional x, add an equality test to x and xor the correction bit. This costs O(E_N N) gates.
Thus C(H_N^{SAT})<=S_D+O(E_N N). If S_D<N^{1+epsilon-delta} and E_N<N^{epsilon-delta}, the claimed source lower bound C(H_N^{SAT})>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} is false.
Hence a nonfunctional proof object that escapes label-functional naturalization must still prove residual hardness after deleting N^{epsilon-o(1)} rows; otherwise it supplies its own falsifier.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No current proof supplies a uniform logarithmic-projection cluster with DirectClusterSound(C,k) for SAT lower bounds. The gap is local target soundness, not proof length or global PCP soundness.
steps: Fix length m and a uniformly generated cluster C of verifier rows; define P_C by existentially projecting the proof variables read by C.
Completeness gives one accepting assignment to the target coordinates U_X(C), namely TT(SAT_m)|U_X(C), so every extension outside U_X(C) lies in P_C; hence density at least 2^{-d}.
Given a tree decomposition of the view-CSP of bag size b, decide membership in P_C by standard dynamic programming over proof variables and the d target constants read from x.
Assume DirectClusterSound(C,k). Then no truth table of an m^k-size circuit belongs to P_C, so P_C is useful against SIZE_m(m^k).
At d,b=O(log N), the property is simultaneously polynomial-density, poly(N)-constructive, and useful against the named target class; therefore the lower-bound route enters natural-proof/PRF pressure.

Test the tempting replacement of DirectClusterSound by ordinary soundness using odd-charge Tseitin parity checks. Every proper local cluster is satisfiable although the full proof view is inconsistent, so ordinary soundness does not imply usefulness.

assumptions: Uniformity regime: row predicates and the row-cluster generator are computable in poly(N), and the tree decomposition is output or checkable in poly(N).
Completeness regime: the intended hard truth table, e.g. TT(SAT_m), has a proof whose restriction to U_P(C) makes all rows in C accept.
Constructivity regime: membership in P_C is decided from x|U_X(C) by dynamic programming over the displayed tree decomposition, not by hidden advice about a small circuit.
Naturalness regime: d<=A log_2 N and b<=B log_2 N for fixed constants A,B, so density and recognition time are polynomial in N.
Same-target regime: usefulness is quantified against exactly SIZE_m(m^k) on the same input length m; no padding, advice, or verifier-length change is allowed.
definitions: source object: A proof-mediated local verifier family V_m(x,pi;r), where x in {0,1}^N is the truth table of an m-bit Boolean function, N=2^m, pi is a long auxiliary proof, and row r reads target coordinates Q_r and proof cells E_r.
target object: SIZE_m(m^k), the nonuniform Boolean circuits on m inputs with at most m^k gates, represented by their N-bit truth tables.

controlled interface: A finite row cluster C with target union U_X(C)=union_{r in C} Q_r, proof variables U_P(C)=union_{r in C} E_r, view-CSP constraints A_r(x|Q_r,pi|E_r)=1, and an explicit tree decomposition of the variable-constraint graph with bag size b.

target-preserving condition: DirectClusterSound(C,k) holds: for every g in TT(SIZE_m(m^k)), no assignment to U_P(C) makes every row in C accept when x=TT(g), and C is generated from m without circuit-dependent advice.
P_C is the projection property {x in {0,1}^N : exists pi_{U_P(C)} such that all constraints in C accept}.
d=|U_X(C)| is the target-query union size; b is the maximum number of binary variables in a tree-decomposition bag.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The positive direction still requires constructing a generated row family with semdim_ad(T_m)>=theta, which is equivalent up to o(1) to proving genuine unrestricted row hardness.
steps: Fix m and a row T_m of length N=2^m with claimed CC(T_m)>2^{theta m}.
Assume an adaptive semantic cover: router R sends x to a leaf family l, a ranked leaf id y, and a local coordinate z.
Hardwire all payload strings for all leaves; their total size in family l is at most 2^{(a_l+mu_l+o(1))m}.
Hardwire the shared opener circuits O_l and the router R. The circuit on input x computes (l,y,z), selects the hardwired payload for y, runs O_l, and outputs T_m(x).
The resulting unrestricted circuit has size dominated by max{tau,max_l(a_l+mu_l),max_l omega_l}, proving the upper bound.
Therefore a cover exponent strictly below theta is a concrete falsifier for the MCSP no-side source, including adaptive Merkle, checkpoint, digest, and proof-opening repairs.

Validity regime check: the derivation uses the definitions and assumptions listed in the candidate lemmas, preserves the same source object and target object, and is valid only in the stated P vs NP branch model with its declared circuit class, length regime, and advice/uniformity conditions.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a route-specific no-go and audit theorem only. It does not prove P != NP and does not construct the required MCSP hard carrier.

assumptions: Circuit model is unrestricted fan-in-2 Boolean circuits with nonuniform hardwiring allowed for each m.
The router maps each input x in {0,1}^m to a leaf identifier and local coordinate using size 2^{tau m+o(m)}.
Leaf family l contains at most 2^{a_l m+o(m)} leaves, and each leaf carries at most 2^{mu_l m+o(m)} summary bits.
The opener for family l has size 2^{omega_l m+o(m)} and computes the row bit from the leaf payload and local coordinate.
The cover may be found by a nonuniform auditor; for a falsifier, existence of the cover already gives a nonuniform circuit upper bound.
The lemma is a route-level no-go for carrier sources, not a proof or disproof of P versus NP.
definitions: source object: generated MCSP anti-ball carrier row T_m in {0,1}^{2^m}, optionally arising from a row/proof stream G_m with low distinct-image entropy D.
target object: E-uniform language L_T whose length-m truth table is T_m, with intended unrestricted circuit lower bound CC(T_m)>2^{theta m}.

controlled interface: adaptive semantic block-cover consisting of a small router, ranked leaf families, hardwired leaf payload summaries, and shared openers that recover T_m(x) from the leaf payload and local coordinate.

target-preserving condition: row lengths are advice-free and kappa-gap searchable, the image entropy overhead D is charged, and the extraction target is only delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)) after the MCSP no-side claim survives all cover falsifiers.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Exhibit a valid generated carrier with CC(T_m)>2^{theta m} and no adaptive semantic cover of exponent below theta; otherwise any discovered subthreshold cover refutes the source, not P != NP.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns adaptive routing, Merkle-like openings, checkpoint trees, and semantic summaries into one finite falsifier gate for MCSP carrier proposals.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Adaptive semantic-cover falsifier. Let T_m be a generated truth-table row claimed to be on the no-side of MCSP at threshold 2^{theta m}. If T_m has an adaptive semantic cover with routing exponent tau, leaf-family count exponents a_l, per-leaf payload exponents mu_l, and shared opener exponents omega_l, and alpha_ad=max{tau,max_l(a_l+mu_l),max_l omega_l}<theta, then the claimed MCSP no-side source is invalid because T_m has unrestricted circuits of size 2^{(alpha_ad+o(1))m}.

assumptions: The opening protocol has a bounded or subexponential description tree whose routing circuit is counted by tau.
All summaries or digests used to answer a block of row positions are hardwirable payloads counted by a_l+mu_l.
No promise is made that the proof stream is natural or dense; the obstruction is a direct nonuniform upper bound.
Randomized openings are fixed to an accepting randomness string only when that string is part of the source certificate and not advice-selected after seeing T_m.

Validity/model regime: this lemma is interpreted only within the stated P vs NP branch model, with the same source object, target object, circuit class, length regime, and advice/uniformity assumptions used by the branch output.
definitions: source object: deterministic row/proof generator G_m that emits a truth-table row T_m and auxiliary proof material P_m.
target object: the same row T_m used as a source for an E lower bound through the MCSP carrier extraction theorem.
controlled interface: syntactic proof openings are translated into router circuits, leaf payloads, and local openers without preserving the proof system syntax.
target-preserving condition: the translation is used only as a falsifier; it preserves the target because any resulting upper bound is an unrestricted circuit for the actual row.

equations.valid_when: Valid when each syntactic opening component has a deterministic semantic role as router, payload, or opener for row bits.

equations.label: leakage-condition

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Closes an obligation by reducing heterogeneous leakage tests to a parameterized normal-form audit.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Any deterministic generated proof stream that opens row bits through bounded adaptive routing, digest recursion, checkpoint summaries, or block witnesses induces an adaptive semantic cover with exponent equal to the largest storage, routing, or opener exponent. Thus many proposed proof-mediated MCSP carriers can be audited by computing one alpha_ad.

assumptions: The cover model allows a one-leaf cover whose opener is any unrestricted circuit for T_m.
Conversely, every cover is flattened by hardwiring its payloads and composing the router with the appropriate opener.
The o(1) term hides polynomial factors in m and constant-depth bookkeeping, not exponential advice leakage.
This boundary is a diagnosis of route difficulty, not a lower bound theorem.
definitions: source object: an individual truth-table row T_m from a low-D generated carrier family.
target object: a lower bound CC(T_m)>2^{theta m} sufficient for the conditional MCSP-to-E transfer after kappa and D losses.
controlled interface: semdim_ad measures the best adaptive semantic cover and therefore exactly captures all nonuniform opening, summary, and circuit-compression leakage.
target-preserving condition: equality is interpreted at fixed m with unrestricted circuits, so it does not introduce a uniform selector or a dense natural property.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A genuine escape must give a non-large, advice-free proof of semdim_ad(T_m)>=theta without converting into a natural property or a hidden selector.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents a false promotion: absence of semantic covers is a lower-bound obligation, not an independent bridge lemma.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Define semdim_ad(T_m) as the infimum adaptive semantic-cover exponent for T_m. Up to o(1), semdim_ad(T_m) equals the unrestricted circuit exponent of T_m. Hence proving semdim_ad(T_m)>=theta is not a cheap certificate; it is a non-natural restatement of the needed row lower bound in cover normal form.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: As mu drops below theta-a for a leaf family of exponent a, the computed alpha_ad=max{tau,a+mu,omega} crosses below theta and the proof stream becomes an explicit falsifier. gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch needs a finite falsifier probe for proof-stream repairs, not another abstract hardness-magnification statement. Adaptive covers directly test whether a proposed generated MCSP anti-ball source leaks a nonuniform circuit for its own row.
